benefits: Skips boilerplate: paste an API response and get compilable classes in seconds.
Infers smart types: integers vs longs, doubles, booleans, DateTime, and nested Lists.
Names things well: keys become PascalCase properties, nested objects become named classes.
Handles edge cases: empty arrays, nulls, and mixed arrays get safe fallback types.
Runs fully in your browser: proprietary API payloads are never uploaded anywhere.

faqs.a: It walks your JSON and emits one C# class per object: each key becomes a public auto-property with an inferred type, nested objects become their own classes, and arrays become List<T>.
faqs.q: How does JSON to C# work?

faqs.a: Whole numbers become int (or long beyond ±2,147,483,647), decimals become double, true/false becomes bool, text becomes string, and ISO-8601 date strings become DateTime.
faqs.q: How are JSON types mapped to C# types?

faqs.a: It inspects the items: if every item has the same inferred type you get List<that>; if items differ or the array is empty you get the safe fallback List<object>.
Each nested object becomes its own class named after its key in PascalCase (address -> Address). Name clashes get a numeric suffix automatically.
Yes. Type the namespace (for example MyApp.Models) and the classes are wrapped in a namespace block. Leave it empty for no namespace.
It is a starting point, not a finished model: add [JsonPropertyName] attributes, nullability, or validation to taste. Always review generated code before shipping.

json-c.formula:
value -> C# type:
  integer (|v| <= 2,147,483,647) -> int, larger -> long
  decimal                        -> double
  true / false                   -> bool
  "text"                         -> string (ISO-8601 date -> DateTime)
  null                           -> object
  [T, T, ...]                    -> List<T>  (mixed/empty -> List<object>)
  { ... }                        -> nested class named after the key
key "created_at" -> property CreatedAt (PascalCase)
howTo: Paste your JSON into the input box - a sample document is preloaded.
Set the root class name (default: Root) and optionally a namespace like MyApp.Models.
The C# classes generate live below the options.
Review the inferred types: adjust DateTime detection or nullability as needed.
Copy the code or download it as a .cs file and drop it into your project.
keyFacts: JSON to C# converts any JSON document into C# classes with auto-properties.
Every object becomes a class; every key becomes a public { get; set; } property in PascalCase.
Integers map to int/long, decimals to double, booleans to bool, ISO-8601 strings to DateTime.
Arrays become List<T> with the item type inferred; mixed or empty arrays fall back to List<object>.
Null values become object; nested objects become named classes with automatic de-duplication.
An optional namespace wraps the output; usings for System and System.Collections.Generic are included.
json-c.keywords: json to c#, json to csharp, convert json to c# classes, json c# class generator, json to poco
limitations: Type inference reads one sample: a field that is sometimes a string and sometimes a number needs manual fixing.
Null gives object and ambiguous dates stay string - review DateTime guesses before shipping.
Generated code has no attributes ([JsonPropertyName]), nullability annotations, or validation - add your own.
Very deep or huge documents produce many classes; consider splitting them manually.
